questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Power factor is defined as the ratio of:
questions.explanation: Power factor is the ratio of true power to apparent power. The source also defines it as cosine of phase angle.
explanationLines: Power factor is the ratio of true power to apparent power.
The source also defines it as cosine of phase angle.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: The ideal power factor of a purely resistive circuit is:
questions.explanation: In a resistive circuit, voltage and current are in phase. So the power factor is unity.
explanationLines: In a resistive circuit, voltage and current are in phase.
So the power factor is unity.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: A low power factor indicates that the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Low power factor means more current for same useful power. Reactive current becomes high in such circuits.
explanationLines: Low power factor means more current for same useful power.
Reactive current becomes high in such circuits.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which of the following devices is commonly used to improve power factor?
questions.explanation: The unit gives static capacitor for power factor correction. It supplies leading current to neutralize lagging effect.
explanationLines: The unit gives static capacitor for power factor correction.
It supplies leading current to neutralize lagging effect.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Power factor in an AC circuit can be improved by:
questions.explanation: The source says capacitor improves low power factor. It draws current leading the voltage.
explanationLines: The source says capacitor improves low power factor.
It draws current leading the voltage.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: In a purely inductive or capacitive circuit, the power factor is:
questions.explanation: In pure reactive circuits, true power is zero. So power factor becomes zero.
explanationLines: In pure reactive circuits, true power is zero.
So power factor becomes zero.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: The power factor of a circuit with a leading power factor indicates the presence of:
questions.explanation: The source says p.f. is leading in capacitive circuit. Capacitor current leads voltage.
explanationLines: The source says p.f. is leading in capacitive circuit.
Capacitor current leads voltage.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: What happens when the power factor of a system is unity?
options: Both reactive and real power flow equally

optionMap.C: Both reactive and real power flow equally

questions.explanation: Unity p.f. means true power equals apparent power. Reactive power is not dominant.
explanationLines: Unity p.f. means true power equals apparent power.
Reactive power is not dominant.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: In a practical power system, a lagging power factor is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: The source says p.f. is lagging in an inductive circuit. AC motors and transformers cause lagging power factor.
explanationLines: The source says p.f. is lagging in an inductive circuit.
AC motors and transformers cause lagging power factor.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: The disadvantages of a low power factor include:
questions.explanation: Low p.f. causes high current. High current increases losses and voltage drop.
explanationLines: Low p.f. causes high current.
High current increases losses and voltage drop.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Power factor correction is typically done by:
questions.explanation: The source lists synchronous condensers for p.f. correction. It also lists static capacitors.
explanationLines: The source lists synchronous condensers for p.f. correction.
It also lists static capacitors.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: The device used to measure power factor is called:
questions.explanation: The measurement device is power factor meter. It directly indicates the power factor.
explanationLines: The measurement device is power factor meter.
It directly indicates the power factor.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: The power factor is lagging in:
questions.explanation: The source states p.f. lags in inductive circuit. Inductive loads are common cause of lagging p.f.
explanationLines: The source states p.f. lags in inductive circuit.
Inductive loads are common cause of lagging p.f.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which formula meaning best matches power factor in the source?
options: Cosine of angle between current and voltage
Ratio of lamp spacing to height

optionMap.A: Cosine of angle between current and voltage
optionMap.D: Ratio of lamp spacing to height

questions.correctOptionText: Cosine of angle between current and voltage
questions.explanation: Power factor is cosine of lead or lag angle. The angle is between current and voltage.
explanationLines: Power factor is cosine of lead or lag angle.
The angle is between current and voltage.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which other definition of power factor is given?
options: Ratio of lumen to watt only
Ratio of service charge to unit

optionMap.B: Ratio of lumen to watt only
optionMap.C: Ratio of service charge to unit

questions.explanation: The source gives p.f. as resistance/impedance. It also gives true power/apparent power ratio.
explanationLines: The source gives p.f. as resistance/impedance.
It also gives true power/apparent power ratio.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: What is quality factor according to the unit?
questions.explanation: The source defines quality factor as reciprocal of power factor. So it increases when p.f. decreases.
explanationLines: The source defines quality factor as reciprocal of power factor.
So it increases when p.f. decreases.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which load gives leading power factor?
questions.explanation: The source says p.f. is leading in capacitive circuit. Capacitor current leads voltage.
explanationLines: The source says p.f. is leading in capacitive circuit.
Capacitor current leads voltage.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which load gives lagging power factor?
questions.explanation: The source says p.f. lags in an inductive circuit. Transformers and AC motors are examples.
explanationLines: The source says p.f. lags in an inductive circuit.
Transformers and AC motors are examples.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which equipment is listed as a cause of low power factor?
questions.explanation: Transformers and AC motors operate at lagging p.f. They are listed as causes of low p.f.
explanationLines: Transformers and AC motors operate at lagging p.f.
They are listed as causes of low p.f.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which lamp type is listed as operating at low power factor?
questions.explanation: The source lists arc lamp and discharge lamps. They operate at low power factor.
explanationLines: The source lists arc lamp and discharge lamps.
They operate at low power factor.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which industrial furnace is listed as very lagging p.f. load?
questions.explanation: The source lists arc and induction furnaces. They operate at very lagging power factor.
explanationLines: The source lists arc and induction furnaces.
They operate at very lagging power factor.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: What happens to current when power factor is low for the same power and voltage?
questions.explanation: For same load and voltage, low p.f. causes high current. The source explains high current affects the system.
explanationLines: For same load and voltage, low p.f. causes high current.
The source explains high current affects the system.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which equipment rating increases due to low power factor?
questions.explanation: The source says transformer and generator rating is affected. More kVA is needed for same output.
explanationLines: The source says transformer and generator rating is affected.
More kVA is needed for same output.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Why does conductor size increase at low power factor?
questions.explanation: Low p.f. makes cables carry more current. The source says wire size must increase to maintain current density.
explanationLines: Low p.f. makes cables carry more current.
The source says wire size must increase to maintain current density.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which effect of low power factor reduces system efficiency?
questions.explanation: Low p.f. causes more energy loss. This results in poor efficiency.
explanationLines: Low p.f. causes more energy loss.
This results in poor efficiency.

questions.subject: utilization-of-electrical-energy
questions.question: Which voltage effect is caused by low power factor?
questions.explanation: The source says low p.f. causes large voltage drops. These occur in generators, transformers and lines.
explanationLines: The source says low p.f. causes large voltage drops.
These occur in generators, transformers and lines.
